pos.personaBrief: Clough wanted football played on the floor with good passing (Anderson), but never framed it as possession control; Forest were a balanced side, not ball-hoarders.

pro.personaBrief: Short passing on the floor, safe players and no wasted hurry; sources say play was on the floor, with forwards holding up until midfield support arrived.

est.personaBrief: Clough fixed roles for players (Wilson) and kept things simple with stable roles, though he disliked blackboard diagrams; the 4-3-3 was flexible with midfielders roaming.

lar.personaBrief: Forest 1977/78 used Robertson's crosses to Woodcock and Withe and Francis was played on the wing, so wide delivery mattered.

blo.personaBrief: Little evidence of pressing; Forest were compact and pragmatic, with a solid back four, and never changed tactics much.

mar.personaBrief: No source on marking scheme; the team gave clear duties to each player and was not concerned with the opponent's stars.

pla.personaBrief: McGovern: tactics never changed much; O'Neill: everything tailored to what we could do, opponents seldom discussed; players were fitted to his roles.

res.personaBrief: Clough wanted to win but through football played the right way, on the floor and entertaining; he was ambitious away and not a defensive closer.

sis.personaBrief: Players were chosen to fit fixed roles, everyone did their job, and stars were not excused; but he also bought talent.

jog.personaBrief: He signed hard men like Burns, Lloyd and Mackay yet wanted technique on the floor; physical but not athletic-pressing.

bas.personaBrief: He bought experienced players such as Shilton, Lloyd, Clark and Gemmill to help the young; he also bought rather than relied on an academy.

lid.personaBrief: Ruled by fear and discipline (Wilson), the boss with no exceptions for stars, with psychology as a weapon.
